sonnet.problem: The statement opens with 'With all those animals and servants,' which makes Job's possessions the reason he is the greatest man. Job 1:3 lists the possessions and then says he was the greatest man, but never gives that as the reason.
sonnet.rule: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

sonnet.problem: The statement bundles two claims: that the first messenger finishes, and that Job has a moment to take in the news. The second claim is invented. Job 1:16 only says another messenger came 'While he was still speaking.'
sonnet.rule: True or false: a statement the baker marks true or false. A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: This re-asks the 'while he was still speaking, another arrives' pattern already tested in card 4 and stated in card 7's question. It is the same point a third time, and the earlier cards let the baker infer the answer.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what Job 'means' by being born and dying naked. Job 1:21 does not say what the line stands for, so the card picks one meaning as the right answer and leaves out the others.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: ... This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.
